original_question: Explain the origin of macroquantization in astrophysics and celestial motion: determine why Bohr-Sommerfeld-type quantization appears to predict planetary and other large-scale orbits, and decide whether its physical origin lies in scale relativity, macroquantum condensates or superfluid vortices, turbulence, logarithmic interactions, or some deeper unifying mechanism.
target_in_paper: No numbered conjecture or theorem in this paper matches the draft; the nearest official formulation is Appendix B, whose abstract says that “the cosmological origin of this macroquantization remains an open question,” and whose introduction narrows the candidate explanations to (a) Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization, (b) macroquantum condensate/superfluid vortices, and (c) cosmic turbulence/logarithmic-type interaction. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already close to the paper’s actual intent: it targets the origin of macroquantization in astrophysics and celestial motion, treats Bohr-Sommerfeld-type quantization as the operative starting point, names essentially the same explanatory families discussed in Appendix B, and preserves the paper’s suggestion that there may be a linkage among them or a deeper theory behind them. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s operational notion of “macroquantization” is not generic large-scale quantization; it is specifically the claimed quantization of celestial motion, especially planetary or exoplanet orbit radii/semimajor axes. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

A stand-alone formulation should state the explicit Bohr-Sommerfeld condition used in the paper: the closed-orbit integral ∮_Γ p·dx = 2πnh, where Γ is a closed classical orbit, p is the momentum, and n = 1,2,3,.... ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

It should also state the derived orbital law that the paper is trying to explain: combining Newtonian force balance GMm/r^2 = mv^2/r with mvr = ng/(2π) yields r_n = n^2GM/v_0^2, where r is the orbit radius or semimajor axis, G is Newton’s constant, M is the central mass, and v_0 is a “specific velocity.” ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

If Nottale’s scale-relativity language is used, the paper treats it as an extension of the Bohr-Sommerfeld approach, not as a wholly separate unrelated mechanism; it gives the equivalent law a_n = GMn^2/v_0^2 and notes v_0 = 144 km/s for the Solar System and exoplanet systems. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The paper does not claim to settle or “decide” the mechanism; it explicitly says that determining which candidate is most consistent with observation is beyond the article’s scope and instead calls for further research to measure the reliability of the competing arguments. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

A paper-faithful rewrite should mention the observational program emphasized in the abstract and conclusion: the proposition should be verified or refuted by further data, particularly exoplanet observations. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The “deeper unifying mechanism” language is faithful only if tied to the paper’s precise claims that there is “perhaps some linkage” among the candidate arguments and that macroquantization may require “a new kind of theory” to explain its origin. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or analogous algebraic hypotheses occur here; Appendix B poses a phenomenological physical open problem, so a self-contained rewrite should avoid importing algebraic assumptions that the paper never states. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
refined_question: Assuming that the reported Bohr-Sommerfeld-type quantization of celestial motion is a genuine empirical effect—namely, that for a body orbiting a central mass M the closed-orbit condition ∮_Γ p·dx = 2πnh (with Γ a closed classical orbit, p the momentum, and n = 1,2,3,...) together with Newtonian force balance GMm/r^2 = mv^2/r leads to a quantized semimajor-axis law r_n = a_n = n^2GM/v_0^2 (where G is Newton’s constant and v_0 a specific velocity)—what is the physical origin of this macroquantization in astrophysics and celestial motion? More specifically, which explanation is most consistent with the observed planetary and exoplanet orbital data: (i) the Bohr-Sommerfeld/Nottale scale-relativity framework itself, (ii) a macroquantum-condensate or superfluid-vortex model of the vacuum or cosmos, (iii) cosmic turbulence with logarithmic-type interaction, or (iv) a deeper theory linking these mechanisms; and what observations would verify or refute these alternatives?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent operational formulation from the paper: if the observed semimajor-axis law a_n = GMn^2/v_0^2 is taken as the phenomenon to be explained, and since the paper states that Nottale’s law “corresponds exactly” to the Bohr-Sommerfeld/Newtonian radius law r_n = n^2GM/v_0^2, what physical mechanism generates this quantized orbital law in celestial systems? ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
justification: This is the narrowest paper-faithful rewrite because Appendix B does not present a formal theorem or numbered conjecture; it presents an open explanatory problem. The abstract identifies the issue as the unexplained “cosmological origin” of reported celestial macroquantization and recommends observational tests, especially on exoplanets. The introduction then lists exactly three candidate explanatory programs. The Bohr-Sommerfeld section supplies the concrete mathematical content of the phenomenon via ∮_Γ p·dx = 2πnh and the resulting radius law r_n = n^2GM/v_0^2; it also says that Nottale’s scale-relativity formula a_n = GMn^2/v_0^2 corresponds exactly to this law. The later sections supply the other two candidate mechanisms—macroquantum condensate/superfluid vortices and cosmic turbulence/logarithmic interaction—while the conclusion explicitly declines to choose among them and suggests that a “new kind of theory” may be needed. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
